extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent owners/practitioners involved in ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing panel conferences, after-final practice, amendment entry, appeal practice (notice, brief, defective briefs, SNQ review), examiner's answer, oral hearings, Board decisions, and post-decision actions in ex parte reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel process (three-person conference and initials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must inform their managers of their intent to issue an Office action. The manager will convene a panel and the members will confer and review the patentability of the claim(s). If the conference confirms the examiner’s preliminary decision to reject and/or allow the claims, the Office action shall be issued and signed by the examiner, with the two, or more, other conferees initialing the action (as 'conferee') to indicate their participation in the conference. All conferees will initial, even though one of them may have dissented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the conference does not confirm the examiner’s preliminary decision, examiner will reevaluate and issue an appropriate Office action. Initialing by conferees is the record that panel review occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Each conference will provide a forum to assist the assigned examiner in considering all issues of patentability as well as procedural issues having an impact on patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conferences are intended to diminish the perception that one examiner disproportionately influences the examiner in charge, provide assurance that all matters are appropriately addressed, give benefit of review from three examiners' perspectives, and provide for a comprehensive discussion of, and finding for, each issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to hold conference
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner issues an Office action without panel review, the patent owner or third party requester who wishes to object must promptly file a paper alerting the Office of this fact. Challenges must be made within two weeks of receipt of the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The absence of conferees' initials evidences lack of panel review. The failure to hold a panel review conference, by itself, is not grounds for vacating Office decision(s) or restarting the reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-final practice — final action concludes prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution before the examiner in a reexamination proceeding will be concluded with the final action. Once a final rejection that is not premature has been entered, the patent owner no longer has any right to unrestricted further prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments submitted after final rejection and prior to, or with, the appeal are governed by strict standards of 37 CFR 1.116. Amendments submitted after appeal are governed by 37 CFR 41.33. Both examiner and patent owner should identify and develop all issues prior to the final Office action, including the presentation of evidence under 37 CFR 1.131(a) and 1.132, because substantial patent rights will be at issue and refiling opportunities are limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to reopen or to enter amendment (37 CFR 1.181)
rubrics_metrics.description: If patent owner believes (A) a final rejection is improper or premature, or (B) an amendment submitted after final complies with 37 CFR 1.116 but examiner improperly refused entry, the patent owner may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 requesting withdrawal of the final rejection and reopening of prosecution, or requesting entry of the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must be filed within the time period for filing a notice of appeal. Filing a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 does not toll the time period for filing a notice of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for response to a final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory period for response to a final rejection in a reexamination proceeding will normally be two (2) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In ex parte reexaminations and certain requested or Director-ordered reexaminations, the time period is automatically extended by two months (per MPEP § 2265) if the response is the first response after the final rejection and a notice of appeal has not yet been filed. Any timely first response (even informal or unsigned) automatically results in the extension of the shortened statutory period for an additional two months. The period for response may not be extended to run past six months from the date of the final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time beyond two months
rubrics_metrics.description: The present practice of providing an automatic two-month extension is in conformance with the Patent Law Treaty; additional 'no cause' extensions of time for filing a response to a final Office action in patent owner requested or Director ordered reexaminations are not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any extensions of time for more than two months from the time for response set in the final rejection must provide a showing of sufficient cause in accordance with 37 CFR 1.550(c)(3). See MPEP § 2265, subsections VI–VII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed after final — criteria for entry
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner cannot, as a matter of right, amend any finally rejected claims, add new claims after a final rejection, or reinstate previously canceled claims. For an amendment filed after final rejection and prior to the appeal brief, a showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b) is required and will be evaluated by the examiner, except where an amendment merely cancels claims, adopts examiner's suggestions, removes issues for appeal, or otherwise requires only a cursory review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment filed after final rejection but before an appeal brief may be entered only if: (A) the total effect is to cancel claims or comply with a previous form requirement, or present rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal; or (B) for an amendment touching the merits, the patent owner provides a showing of good and sufficient reasons why the amendment is necessary and was not earlier presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: First proposed amendment after final — examiner consideration and explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: The first proposed amendment after final action in a reexamination proceeding will be given sufficient consideration to determine whether it places all the claims in condition where they are patentable and/or whether the issues on appeal are reduced or simplified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless the proposed amendment is entered in its entirety, the examiner will briefly explain the reasons for not entering a proposed amendment (e.g., if the claims as amended present a new issue requiring further consideration or search, the new issue should be identified and a brief explanation provided). Patent owner should be notified if portions of the amendment would be entered if submitted separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling omissions and defective/informal responses after final
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of giving a time period to supply an omission (MPEP § 2266.01) or notifying defects via PTOL-475 or PTO-2311 (MPEP § 2266.02) does not apply after a final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a bona fide response filed after final rejection omits a necessary point, the examiner should not issue a notice of failure to fully respond; instead an advisory Office action (e.g., form PTOL-467) should be issued explaining the omission or defect. Examiners should not issue PTOL-475 or PTO-2311 after final rejection; use PTOL-467 for explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of appeal — who may appeal and filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may appeal to the Board only after the final rejection of the claims. A third party requester may not appeal or participate in the patent owner's appeal. The notice of appeal need not be signed. The fee set forth in 37 CFR 41.20(b)(1) must accompany the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period for filing the notice of appeal is the period set for response in the last Office action (normally 2 months). A timely first response to a final rejection with a shortened period is construed as including a request to extend the period for response an additional two months, so long as the total period does not exceed six months from the date of final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief content and formatting (37 CFR 41.37)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant shall file a brief of the authorities and arguments relied on to maintain the appeal, including a summary of claimed subject matter which must refer to the specification by page and line number, and to the drawing, if any, by reference characters, and a copy of the claims involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one copy of the appeal brief is required. In reexamination, copy of claims on appeal must include all underlining and bracketing as required by 37 CFR 1.530(f) to reflect changes made during reexamination. Any new claims added in reexamination should be completely underlined. Where a third-party requester exists, a copy of the brief must be served on that requester. The brief and all appeal papers should indicate the art unit and reexamination control number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness and completeness of appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: It is essential the Board be provided with a brief fully stating the position of the appellant with respect to each issue involved in the appeal so that no search of the record is required to determine that position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefs must be responsive to every ground of rejection stated by the examiner. A lack of argument versus unconvincing argument: lack of any argument justifies summarily sustaining the rejection, whereas unconvincing arguments receive a decision on the merits (likely an affirmance). Reply briefs, if filed, shall be entered, but amendments/affidavits/evidence are subject to 37 CFR 1.116 and 41.33.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board responsibility for defective appeal briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Since May 25, 2010, the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (Board) has the sole responsibility for determining whether appeal briefs in ex parte reexamination proceedings comply with 37 CFR 41.37, and will complete the determination before the brief is forwarded to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board finds a brief compliant or only with minor informalities, it will accept and forward it. If non-compliant, the Board will send a notice requiring a corrected brief within the time set in the notice or the appeal may be dismissed. Examiners are no longer to hold appeal briefs defective; the Board handles notifications (e.g., PTOL-462R). If serious defects prevent drafting an examiner's answer, the examiner should report to the Director of CRU who will communicate with the Board as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to traverse grounds of rejection in brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must traverse every ground of rejection set forth in the final rejection that appellant is presenting for review in the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral argument at the hearing will not remedy failure to traverse a ground of rejection in the brief. Ignoring or acquiescing in any rejection, even formal matters which could be cured by amendment, will invite summarily affirmance of the rejection. Failure to timely file notice/fee results in dismissal (use PTOL-468) and termination of reexamination prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeking Board review of a finding of a Substantial New Question (SNQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may seek review of the examiner's SNQ determination before the Board along with any appeal of the examiner's rejections, but to obtain review of the SNQ issue the patent owner must have first requested reconsideration before the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To preserve right to Board review, include the SNQ issue and appropriate arguments in the appeal brief, present the SNQ under a separate heading, and identify the communication in which reconsideration was first requested. For ex parte reexaminations ordered prior to June 25, 2010 the Board panel will review the procedural SNQ issue if presented in the appeal brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's answer — content and new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary examiner may furnish a written answer to the appeal brief. An examiner's answer is deemed to incorporate all grounds of rejection set forth in the Office action from which the appeal is taken (as modified by advisory actions and pre-appeal conference decisions) unless the answer expressly indicates a ground has been withdrawn. An examiner's answer may include a new ground of rejection if it relies upon evidence not relied upon in the Office action; approval of the Director is required to furnish an answer that includes a new ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP §§ 1207–1207.05 relate to preparation of examiner's answers; pre-appeal conference requirement does not apply in reexamination but panel review of examiner's answer is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant response options to a new ground of rejection in examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner’s answer contains a rejection designated as a new ground of rejection, appellant must within two months from the date of the examiner’s answer choose one of two options to avoid sua sponte dismissal as to the claims subject to the new ground:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Reopen prosecution: request reopening before the primary examiner by filing a reply under § 1.111 with or without amendment or submission of affidavits (§§ 1.130, 1.131, 1.132) or other evidence relevant to the new ground, which will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal; or (2) Maintain appeal: file a reply brief under § 41.41 addressing each new ground of rejection (per § 41.37(c)(1)(iv)); a reply brief may not be accompanied by any amendment, affidavit or other evidence (if it is, treated as reopening prosecution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time relating to examiner's answer and replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time under § 1.136(a) for patent applications are not applicable to the time period set forth for responses to an examiner's answer in this section. See § 1.136(b) and § 1.550(c) for extension guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appellant must observe the two-month deadline to respond to a new ground; other extension rules referenced in MPEP and CFR apply in limited contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing request requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant desires an oral hearing, appellant must file a written request for such hearing accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 41.20(b)(3) within two months after the date of the examiner’s answer or supplemental examiner's answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time for requesting an oral hearing may not be extended. No appellant will be permitted to participate in an oral hearing unless the request and fee are filed. In reexamination proceedings, oral hearings are open to the public as observers unless appellant petitions under 37 CFR 41.3 to close the hearing, presents sufficient reasons, pays the petition fee (37 CFR 41.20(a)), and the petition is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decision and actions following decision — Notices of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: After appeal resolution and expiration of further appeal time, the examiner will take post-decision actions, including preparing a Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) indicating the status of claims at the time of final rejection or after second rejection where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (A) If Board affirms rejection of amended claim 1 and dependent claim 2 was allowable only because of dependency, prepare NIRC indicating claims 1 and 2 are canceled. (B) If all claims rejected and one independent claim reversed while dependent claims depend on a rejected claim, options include converting dependent claim into independent form by examiner’s amendment and canceling affirmed-rejected claims, or setting a 1-month time limit for appellant to rewrite dependent claims in independent form (no extensions under 37 CFR 1.550(c)). If no timely reply, prepare NIRC indicating canceled claims. Allowable dependent claims based on an unamended patent claim that has been rejected/canceled should not be objected to because of dependency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal for failure to timely file notice of appeal or fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner does not timely file a notice of appeal and/or the appropriate appeal fee, the patent owner will be notified that the appeal is dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTOL-468 may be used to notify the patent owner that the appeal is dismissed. The reexamination prosecution is then terminated and a NIRC will subsequently be issued indicating the status of the claims at the time of final rejection.
